chunks: It was said to him (peace be upon him): Describe to us the wise one.
He said (peace be upon him): He is the one who places things in their proper positions.
Then, it was asked: Describe to us the ignorant one.
He said: I have already done so.

key_terms.الْجَاهِلَ: The ignorant one (one lacking proper discernment)
key_terms.الْعَاقِلَ: The wise one (one endowed with intellect and discernment)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of a wise person in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this concise maxim from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) defines the wise person (al-'Aqil) as one who places things in their proper positions (mawadi'ihim), a concept deeply rooted in Shia epistemology where wisdom entails recognizing the inherent value and appropriate context of all entities. When asked to describe the ignorant, he replies 'I have already done so,' implying that the failure to discern these proper placements is the very definition of ignorance, thereby linking intellectual clarity to spiritual and practical order. This brevity reflects the rhetorical style of the Imams, using the description of the positive trait to implicitly define its negation.
